text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: high GPU pool utilization in us-west-2 — free_capacity 2.7% across inference-gpu-pool-3. Queue growth on model redwood-llama-7b-quant_v2. Throttling observed. Auto-scaler failing to add nodes (rate-limited). Root TS 3901234567

maya: seeing a sustained queue spike — 10k pending requests in the last 2m for that model. Latency SLO > 95th. Customers hitting 503s.

samir: confirmed. Dashboards show continuous-batching params were changed 25m ago in the rollout (batch_window reduced from 60ms -> 8ms). Also prefix-cache TTL dropped to 1s in the same change. suspect cache missstorm + smaller batches = throughput collapse.

oncall-tim: paging in. I’m on it. Any immediate mitigation we can flip?

infra-eli: autoscaler logs show API rate limit to cloud provider when requesting new GPU instances: "RateLimitExceeded: too many requests". But even if nodes come up, per-pod concurrency is low because batching params were tightened.

oncall-tim: ok. Plan: 1) Pause continuous-batching change (roll back to previous config). 2) Temporarily increase prefix-cache TTL to 30s. 3) Request emergency reserved GPUs (if autoscaler still blocked). 4) Notify CS about customer impact. I’ll run steps 1-2 now.

maya: tagging the rollout that changed batching: `cfg/serve/redwood-llama-7b/continuous-batching.yaml` revision r2026. Reverting to r2025 reduces throughput regression in canary earlier.

samir: adding commands below — revert and reload cache config.

samir: ```
# revert batching config
git checkout origin/main -- cfg/serve/redwood-llama-7b/continuous-batching.yaml
kubectl apply -f cfg/serve/redwood-llama-7b/continuous-batching.yaml -n inference
# increase prefix cache ttl
kubectl patch configmap prefix-cache-config -n inference --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/PREFIX_TTL","value":"30s"}]'
```

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by samir at 3901234585 — rolling config to inference namespace. Status: in_progress (pods restarting to pick up config).

oncall-tim: running quick smoke: tail logs for a hotspot pod.

oncall-tim: ```
# tail logs
kubectl logs -n inference pod/infer-redwood-7b-abc -f | sed -n '1,120p'
# observed KV cache misses: 98% -> causing recompute on long prefixes
```

infra-eli: opened emergency-capacity request with cloud: case 889227. Requesting 8 gpus on priority. Pending approval; ETA ~ 11m. If cloud denies, we can shift low-priority traffic to older model variant (7b-fp16) but need routing config change.

customer-success-ana: flagging top 3 affected customers in ticketing: acme-ads, bluebook, chatly. They are seeing increased error rates and slow responses. Sending proactive note now.

maya: after revert starting to see batching window increase to ~55ms on canary. Throughput on canary increased x3, queue drain observable.

deploy-bot: config rollout completed at 3901234621. 0/12 pods failing.

oncall-tim: monitoring queue length... it's dropping but still high. current pending 6.2k -> 3.1k over 90s. Latency 95th falling from 4.2s -> 1.6s for canary.

samir: prefix cache TTL patch applied at 3901234630. KV hitrate improved from 22% -> 78% on sampled pods. This reduces per-request tokens and memory churn.

infra-eli: cloud responded to emergency request: approved 4 GPUs immediate, 4 more in 12m. Autoscaler resumed creating nodes.

oncall-tim: good. Initiating traffic weight shift: route 30% of traffic to canary nodes to accelerate queue drain.

maya: executed route change via routing-console: rollout id r-3901234638.

deploy-bot: routing change accepted.

customer-success-ana: sent initial status update to affected customers: short summary, mitigation steps, ETA for full recovery ~30-45m. They replied—some customers requested SLA credits; creating follow-ups.

samir: monitoring metrics: tokens/sec rising, instance GPU utilization trending down as queue drains. Continuous-batching revert is main win. Still watching autoscaler hysteresis and rate-limit backoff.

infra-eli: follow-up: after scale events, we saw one node fail healthchecks due to ephemeral nvram error; drained and replaced automatically. No data loss.

maya: logging incident doc: http://go/inc/3901234567 — add notes and timeline. Anyone who handled steps add short bullet.

oncall-tim: handoff to infra-eli for capacity follow-up and postmortem. I’ll stay for next 20m then hand to morning oncall.

infra-eli: ack. Will verify autoscaler quotas and cloud rate limits. Will file infra action items: 1) backoff tuning for cloud rate limits, 2) emergency reserved capacity playbook, 3) validation on batching/prefix config rollouts (automated canary throughput checks).

customer-success-ana: I'll continue customer comms and collect impact windows.

samir: followed up with PR to add pre-deploy throughput smoke (small load test) to catch regressions like batch window shrink. Link PR: http://go/pull/5312

maya: tl;dr: cause = simultaneous change to continuous-batching and prefix-cache TTL -> batch sizes collapsed + cache missstorm -> per-token compute up -> throughput collapse + autoscaler rate limits delayed capacity add -> customer errors. Mitigations = revert batching change, bump prefix TTL, emergency capacity, route to canary/older model to buy time.

pagerbot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: severity reduced to P2 at 3901234680. Queue draining, customer impact reduced.

oncall-tim: closing live mitigation. Handing to infra-eli for postmortem and to CS for customer remediation. Will open follow-up doc and tag SRE/ML/Platform.

infra-eli: creating postmortem draft. ETA by EOD.

customer-success-ana: will follow up with legal/finance on SLA credit requests.

maya: thanks everyone. If you added quick notes to the incident doc, please include exact commands and timestamps.

samir: added commands, metrics, and graphs to the doc.

pagerbot: incident thread archived at 3901234699."
